extracted.intended_audience: GAP users and package developers (authors of tests, packages, and GAP scripts)
extracted.subtask_short: writing GAP tests and file management
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and options for writing and running GAP .tst tests, controlling test reporting/formatting/timings, managing recursion and garbage collection settings, using the global options stack, and portable file and directory operations within GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: reportDiff
rubrics_metrics.description: A function that gets six arguments and reports a difference in the output: the GAP input, the expected GAP output, the newly generated output, the name of tested file, the line number of the input, the time to run the input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be overwritten to customize how differences are reported. The default behaviour is shown in examples; it may be set to Ignore to suppress printing differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: rewriteToFile (Test)
rubrics_metrics.description: If bound to a string it is considered as a file name and that file is written with the same input and comment lines as the tested file but with outputs substituted by the newly generated version; if bound to true, treated as if bound to the filename; default is false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially useful for generating test files because it ensures that generated test files are formatted exactly as Test expects them to be. Often used to update expected outputs after changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: writeTimings
rubrics_metrics.description: If bound to a string it is considered as a file name; that file is written and contains timing information for each input in the test file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to record per-input timing information for later comparison or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: compareTimings
rubrics_metrics.description: If bound to a string it is considered as the name of a file containing timing information previously stored via writeTimings; the new timings are compared to the stored ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default only commands taking more than 100 milliseconds are considered and only differences greater than 20% are significant. To override defaults assign a list [timingfile, threshold, percentage] to this component. Default value is false.

rubrics_metrics.name: reportTimeDiff
rubrics_metrics.description: Component used to overwrite the default function to display timing differences; must be a function with 5 arguments: GAP input, name of test file, line number, stored time, new time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a custom formatting/handling routine for timing differences when using compareTimings.

rubrics_metrics.name: ignoreSTOP_TEST
rubrics_metrics.description: When true (default) the output of GAP input starting with "STOP_TEST" is not checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to include diagnostic or run-time-only lines in tests that should not be validated against expected output.

rubrics_metrics.name: showProgress (Test and TestDirectory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controls progress reporting during testing. If true prints position info and the input line before processing; if "some" shows the current line number only; if false no progress updates are displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is "some" when GAP’s output goes to a terminal, otherwise false. TestDirectory also accepts showProgress with same semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: subsWindowsLineBreaks
rubrics_metrics.description: If true then GAP substitutes DOS/Windows style line breaks "\r\n" by UNIX style line breaks "\n" after reading the test file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is true. Use to avoid spurious differences when tests are created on Windows but run on Unix-like environments (or vice versa).

rubrics_metrics.name: returnNumFailures
rubrics_metrics.description: If true then GAP returns the number of input lines of the test file which had differences in their output, instead of returning true or false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows programmatic checking of how many test lines failed rather than a boolean pass/fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestDirectory behaviour and inlist argument
rubrics_metrics.description: TestDirectory(inlist[, optrec]) accepts a filename, directory name, or list of such; it will collect files (recursively searching directories for files ending in .tst) and run Test on each file, printing results and returning true if all tests passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TestDirectory to run whole sets of tests. When passing directories the search is recursive and only files ending in .tst are selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestDirectory.testOptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An optional record which, if present, is passed as the second argument of Test for each file processed by TestDirectory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to centrally set Test options (like rewriteToFile, compareTimings, etc.) for a batch run.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestDirectory.earlyStop
rubrics_metrics.description: If true, stop as soon as any Test fails (defaults to false).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable to fail-fast when running many tests to save time or to diagnose first failure quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestDirectory.suppressStatusMessage
rubrics_metrics.description: If true suppress displaying status messages such as "#I Errors detected while testing" and "#I No errors detected while testing" after the test (defaults to false).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for scripting when such status messages are noisy or handled separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestDirectory.rewriteToFile
rubrics_metrics.description: If true, rewrite each test file on disk, substituting outputs by the results of running the test (defaults to false).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with Test.rewriteToFile, especially useful for generating or updating expected outputs across many tests to ensure consistent formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestDirectory.exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of file and directory names which will be excluded from testing (defaults to []).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to omit known-broken tests, large tests, or files not intended for the batch run.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestDirectory.exitGAP
rubrics_metrics.description: If true, instead of returning true/false TestDirectory will exit GAP with return value set to success or fail depending on whether all tests passed (defaults to false).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in CI scripts that rely on GAP's process exit status to indicate overall success/failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: SetRecursionTrapInterval
rubrics_metrics.description: SetRecursionTrapInterval(interval) sets the nesting depth at which GAP will enter the Break loop (recursion trap). interval must be a non-negative small integer (documented range implies a large upper bound).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interval of 0 suppresses recursion monitoring entirely (risky — excessive recursion may crash GAP). Default behavior triggers traps at multiples of 5000 unless changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: GetRecursionDepth
rubrics_metrics.description: GetRecursionDepth() returns the current nesting level of the GAP interpreter; it is reset to 0 every time the break loop is entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to introspect recursion depth for debugging or to report in custom OnBreak handlers. Examples show using it to print depth during deep recursion.

rubrics_metrics.name: CollectGarbage(full)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forces a garbage collection. If full is true triggers a full GC, otherwise a partial one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally unnecessary because GAP runs GC automatically. Introduced in GAP 4.12; older versions use GASMAN("collect") / GASMAN("partial").

rubrics_metrics.name: GasmanStatistics
rubrics_metrics.description: GasmanStatistics() returns a record with up to four components (full, partial, npartial, nfull) providing information about garbage collection events and stats (e.g., livebags, livekb, deadbags, deadkb, freekb, totalkb, time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret results with caution: deadkb and deadbags may overflow with many partial collections; livekb + freekb will usually not sum to totalkb because of memory manager overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: GasmanMessageStatus / SetGasmanMessageStatus
rubrics_metrics.description: GasmanMessageStatus() returns one of "none", "full", or "all" showing which garbage collection messages are printed. SetGasmanMessageStatus(stat) sets this messaging level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to control verbosity of GASMAN messages (none = no messages, full = full collections only, all = all collections). Meaningful only when GASMAN is the garbage collector.

rubrics_metrics.name: GasmanLimits
rubrics_metrics.description: GasmanLimits() returns a record with components min (minimum workspace size in KB set by -m), max (maximum workspace size in KB set by -o; 0 means no limit), and kill (absolute maximum set by -K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If workspace would need to grow past max GAP will enter a break loop to warn the user; workspace will never be allowed to grow past kill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options Stack model
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP supports a global stack of option records; the effective value of an option is given by the topmost record where that field is bound. Intended pattern: PushOptions(rec(...)); DoSomething(args); PopOptions();
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options should guide algorithmic choices without changing mathematical specification. Options pushed remain in effect for all procedures called by the pushing function unless altered. There is no automatic check for misspelt or undefined options.

rubrics_metrics.name: PushOptions and ValueOption semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: PushOptions(options_record) pushes a record of options onto the global option stack. ValueOption(opt) inspects the options stack without changing it and returns the value of opt or fail if not set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pushing rec(opt := fail) effectively resets opt. Functions that might be affected by options should call ValueOption to decide behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: PopOptions and ResetOptionsStack
rubrics_metrics.description: PopOptions() removes the top-most options record. ResetOptionsStack() unbinds all options records from the stack (not intended for use within a function; intended to clean up after quitting from break loops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ResetOptionsStack warns when it does something; OnQuit is typically defined to perform a variant of ResetOptionsStack at startup.

rubrics_metrics.name: OnQuit behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: OnQuit() is called when a user selects to quit via a break loop entered by Error; initially defined to do nothing during start-up and later redefined to warn and clean options stack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides cleanup behaviour when quitting from break loops; not widely advertised because exception handling may make it obsolete.

rubrics_metrics.name: DisplayOptionsStack and InfoOptions
rubrics_metrics.description: DisplayOptionsStack() prints a human-readable display of the complete options stack. InfoOptions is an info class that can enable messages about options being changed (level 1) or accessed (level 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DisplayOptionsStack for debugging option values; use InfoOptions to control diagnostic verbosity related to options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filename portability guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: For portability filenames and directory names should be restricted to at most 8 alphanumerical characters optionally followed by a dot and between 1 and 3 alphanumerical characters; avoid uppercase letters and prefer lower-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some operating systems are case-insensitive or have different filename constraints; following this restriction avoids cross-platform issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directory and ~ expansion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Directory(string) returns a directory object; Directory understands "." for current directory and a leading '~' as a path relative to GAPInfo.UserHome if defined. "~other_user" is not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paths are otherwise taken relative to current directory. Use Directory to construct platform-independent directory objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: DirectoryTemporary guarantees and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: DirectoryTemporary() returns a newly created empty temporary directory object and GAP will attempt to remove it upon termination. If unable to create, fail is returned. A warning is given if more than 1000 temporary directories are created in a session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DirectoryTemporary when creating ephemeral files during tests or package operations; check LastSystemError() on failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: DirectoriesLibrary and Filename(list-of-dirs, name) search semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: DirectoriesLibrary([name]) returns directory objects for named library directories (e.g., "lib","doc","tst"); Filename(list-of-dirs, name) searches the list in order and returns the filename in the first directory containing the file, or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When locating library files use DirectoriesLibrary together with Filename(list, name). To create new files in library-like areas prefer DirectoryTemporary rather than writing into GAP root directories.

rubrics_metrics.name: PathSystemProgram
rubrics_metrics.description: PathSystemProgram(name) returns the path of the first executable file named name in the directories returned by DirectoriesSystemPrograms, or fail if none exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to locate system programs in a cross-platform way (e.g., to find /bin/date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special filenames: *stdin*, *errin*, *stdout*, *errout*
rubrics_metrics.description: Special filenames denote standard streams. "*stdin*" denotes standard input and reading behaviour depends on whether input was redirected; "*errin*" and "*errout*" denote stderr streams (with OS-dependent behaviour); "*stdout*" denotes standard output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that reading *stdin* interacts with terminal EOF semantics and that *errin*/ *errout* may fail or refer to the terminal depending on redirections.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsExistingFile / IsReadableFile / IsWritableFile / IsExecutableFile / IsDirectoryPath
rubrics_metrics.description: File-access predicates that return true/false depending on existence and permissions. IsDirectoryPath(filename) returns true if the filename exists and is a directory (it does not check write/execute permissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When these return false use LastSystemError().message to get OS-provided diagnostic strings. Example behaviours are given for common cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read(filename) semantics and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Read opens filename, reads and evaluates its contents (results not printed). If file doesn't exist or cannot be opened an error is signalled. If a statement in the file causes an error a break loop is entered, and eof is a special symbol — a statement must not begin in one file and end in another. Upper limit of 15 simultaneously open files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with nesting reads and break loops; QUIT or quitting from break loop affects enclosing Reads; use ReadAsFunction to avoid polluting globals when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReadAsFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: ReadAsFunction(filename) reads the file as a function and returns that function; evaluating it does not affect global variables used inside the file because locals are preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to safely execute file contents without side effects on globals (examples show local a unaffected).

rubrics_metrics.name: PrintTo and AppendTo
rubrics_metrics.description: PrintTo(filename[, objs...]) prints objects to filename (overwrites file). AppendTo appends to filename. Files must be writable and an error is signalled otherwise. There is an upper limit of 15 output files open simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PrintTo with only filename argument empties the file. Be careful not to use PrintTo/AppendTo to write to the same logfile used by LogTo.

rubrics_metrics.name: LogTo / InputLogTo / OutputLogTo semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: LogTo(filename) logs the entire interaction (everything printed on terminal) to filename (overwrites). InputLogTo(filename) logs subsequent input only. OutputLogTo(filename) logs subsequent output only. Calling without argument stops logging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LogTo cannot be used at the same time as InputLogTo or OutputLogTo. InputLogTo and OutputLogTo can be used together. Each overwrites existing files.

rubrics_metrics.name: CrcFile
rubrics_metrics.description: CrcFile(filename) computes a CRC checksum for the content of filename and returns it as an integer. Returns fail on error (e.g., file does not exist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for quick content-change detection; see also HexSHA256 for stronger hashes.

rubrics_metrics.name: RemoveFile
rubrics_metrics.description: RemoveFile(filename) removes the named file and returns true on success; returns fail if a system error occurred (use LastSystemError to inspect reason).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check permissions and path existence; errors are signalled by returning fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: UserHomeExpand
rubrics_metrics.description: UserHomeExpand(str) substitutes a leading '~' in str with the user’s home directory as stored in GAPInfo.UserHome; otherwise returns str unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to expand user-home-relative paths in a portable way inside GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reread and REREADING effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Reread(filename) sets the global REREADING flag to true, reads filename, then resets it. When REREADING is true some system functions behave differently: assignment to read-only global variables is permitted; NewRepresentation/NewInfoClass with identical parameters return existing objects; methods may displace existing methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reread is a partial solution for reloading library files but may not produce intended results if representations or method requirements changed; not recommended to use programmatically — sometimes a GAP restart is required.
